To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of carbon fiber composite materials to increase the flexual capacity of reinforced concrete bridge beams is an effective method of strengthening existing concrete bridges.

(1) the use of carbon fiber composite sheets to increase the flexure capacity of existing reinforced concrete bridge beams is a viable option; (2) the CFRP composites must be bonded to the surface of the beam to increase the flexual strength; and (3) the CFRP composite system must be designed so that the CFRP sheets remain bonded to the beam during flexural loading.
CFRP composites are effective in increasing the load capacity of concrete beams and that the CFRP system should be applied in two layers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of carbon fiber composites to increase flexural capacity of existing reinforced concrete bridges.
the use of carbon fiber-reinforced polymers (CFRP) to increase the flexure strength and stiffness of reinforced concrete (RC) beams.
the use of carbon fiber composites to increase flexural capacity of existing concrete bridge beams.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of CFRP to strengthen existing reinforced concrete beams has a high probability of being effective.
the CFRP composites were able to significantly increase the flexural capacities of reinforced concrete beams when the CFRP compositess are applied to the tension side of beams.
CFRP systems can increase the flexural strength of reinforced concrete beams by 20 to 30 percent and that the increase in strength depends on the layout of the composite system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of CFRP composites can significantly increase the flexural strength of reinforced concrete beams and can be used to strengthen existing reinforced concrete bridges.
the CFRP systems were able to increase the ultimate load carrying capacity of the beams by 50 to 100 percent.
the layout of the carbon fiber reinforced polymer system is critical to its effectiveness.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CFRP composites should be applied to the bottom of the beams.
the use of a CFRP system with a layout that is similar to a conventional steel reinforcement pattern will result in a more ductile behavior of the strengthened beams.
the CFRP system must be placed in a manner that prevents debonding of CFRP from the concrete.
